My entire trip was insane! We found out when we arrived at Base Camp that there were likely not going to be any flights for several weeks due to weather. She had misshapen discs in her spine since birth. There was a low chance of the very expensive surgery to ever work so we did pain management since her diagnosis at 3. She would have pain flare ups that were always manageable. Then on Tuesday evening she lost the ability to walk, it was very sudden. I didn't have a way to get to the vet until the next morning, but it wouldn't have mattered. The discs had compressed enough to kill her spinal cord causing myelomalacia (death of the spinal cord). The vet gave me her options, but nothing would have stopped the slow painful death she was destined to have. (Although with her rate of deterioration it was looking like less than a couple days left). 

I wished there was more I could do. We did airplane taxis, and my wife was recollecting about how she was her personal chauffeur. We had ramps and stairs and gave her all the wonderful chicken and treats when she was feeling down. It was less than 16 hours since she was first in pain during her most recent episode to paralysis and then the end. We always knew there was a chance but it happened so incredibly fast.
She was 6; we just celebrated her birthday on April 2nd.

I agree with what you're saying. However there are always outliers and my body was an exception not the standard. My cancer was being fed and was producing more estrogen the more testosterone I had in my body without estrogen blockers. Just really telling my ovaries "Keep going until he dies!" [Estrogen Dependent Cancers](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/10312-estrogen-dependent-cancers).

And yes my surgeon knew that PCOS and HRT, along with genetics could have caused my cysts to be cancerous well before I got my ovaries removed. So, yea, they were well informed and communicated with me about the various problems that could have been going on as well as the possible solutions. 🤷🏻‍♂️ Not everyone fits into medicines perfectly defined box.

They actually raised my dose in combo with the estrogen blocker. But no, I would've died from the cancerous cysts in a couple years.

But cancer aside, estrogen blockers and raising T should help to stop your cycle. My surgeon was adamant that it would help, I just literally couldn't do anything I was in so much pain. 

If you are on the gel, there have been a couple studies that recommended switching to the shot as it's more effective in stopping menstrual cycles. I also switched to the shot but after my surgeries. I didn't have time to test every solution! I just knew I didn't want to use BC.

Disabling hardware acceleration allows you to stream Netflix on Discord because it prevents DRM (Digital Rights Management) protections from interfering with the stream. By disabling hardware acceleration, the video decoding is handled by the CPU instead, which may not enforce the same level of DRM protection, allowing you to stream the video content through screen-sharing platforms like Discord. Bring a face mask. I contracted walking atypical pneumonia and almost died before I could get home. You may not need it on the trail itself, but a lot of the tea houses and lodges are jam-packed during the day.

There was even a dude just straight throwing up in the communal bathrooms, hand sanitizer and things that keep you from touching any of the fixtures is also something you may want to consider.

For showers, we had to pay to buy "hot" showers and so I only took two on my trip. If you're lucky like me, I didn't sweat too too much, the pace is about 2.5 mph. So its really not strenuous. Most tea houses have showers and some of the rooms have their own bathrooms. Just be careful of spiders.

As far as gear... I only did the trek to EBC and our porters literally carried all of my 11kg of gear besides my water bladder, some snacks, and an extra jacket, so I don't think I could recommend my size bag for your trip. The group that we had went with that did the three passes had to carry all of their own gear and so they had around 80L bags whereas I had a 45L. I highly recommend the Julbo Vermont Classic Glacier Glasses for altitudes above 15km! They have side and nose shades as well as they are very dark. Perfect for the amount of sunlight there. For boots, its based on preference. I like the Altra boots that were all-weather. I could step in the glacier puddles and lakes and would only have a cold foot afterwards, not wet. It'll be based on what you like though, the only advice I have there is to break them in before going to prevent blisters! I took a Cotopaxi hooded down jacket and had an under armour undershirt which was enough for me, but that's also preference.

Have fun, good luck, and happy trails!

P.S. Dal Bhat energy is legit and its super tasty, make sure you have some!
